accepted.question_text: Find an example of a nontrivial graph cocycle action on a Poisson bracket, meaning an action that produces a family of inequivalent Poisson structures not related by a coordinate change.

evidence.quote: It remains an open problem to find an example of nontrivial graph cocycle action on a Poisson bracket, thus spreading it to a family of inequivalent structures not related by a coordinate change.

accepted.question_text: For the tetrahedral graph cocycle action on the space of Nambu-Poisson brackets, determine whether the action is nontrivial or instead trivial in the sense of being generated only by a coordinate change.

evidence.quote: Using the Kontsevich-Nambu micro-graphs in dimensions d >= 2, we explore the open problem of (non)triviality for Kontsevich's tetrahedral graph cocycle action on the space of Nambu-Poisson brackets.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the gamma_3-flow is nontrivial, that is, whether the induced change of a Poisson bivector is more than a coordinate change along a vector field X_{gamma_3}^d on R^d.

evidence.quote: Recall the standard problem in deformation theory: is the gamma_3-flow nontrivial, i.e. does the change of Poisson bivector not amount to a change of coordinates along a vector field X gamma_3 d on R d ?

accepted.question_text: Assume that in dimension d+1 the tetrahedral Kontsevich graph flow on a Nambu-Poisson bracket is trivial, meaning the flow Q_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗4}) can be written as the Schouten bracket [[P, X_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗3})]] for some vector field X_{gamma_3}^{d+1}. Determine whether that trivializing vector field can always be constructed as a linear combination of descendants, in dimension d+1, of the two-dimensional 'sunflower' graph.

evidence.quote: If Ṗ = Q gamma3 d+1(P⊗4) is trivial, Q gamma3 d+1 = [[P, X⃗ gamma3 d+1(P⊗3)]], then is X⃗ gamma3 d+1 found over linear combinations of the 'sunflower' descendants from 2D ?

accepted.question_text: If the trivializing vector field X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} for the tetrahedral flow in dimension d+1 can be constructed from sunflower descendants, determine whether it is enough to use the union of two classes of dimension-(d+1) descendants: first, descendants of the previously known dimension-d solution X_{gamma_3}^d, and second, descendants of vanishing one-vector micro-graphs defined over R^d.
accepted.context_brief: Descendants of prior solution and vanishing graphs

evidence.quote: If yes, is X⃗ gamma3 d+1 found over the union of (d + 1)-descendants for the underlying solution X⃗ gamma3 d and vanishing 1-vector micro-graphs over R d ?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the vanishing micro-graphs that are indispensable for constructing and analyzing the dimension-(d+1) problem arise only by taking descendants of an underlying vanishing set already present in dimension d-1, rather than from genuinely new vanishing mechanisms appearing for the first time in higher dimension.

evidence.quote: Do these indispensable (cf. [6]) vanishing micro-graphs stem only from the underlying vanishing set in R d−1 through their descendants ?

accepted.question_text: What is the group-theoretic and topological mechanism of vanishing for Nambu micro-graphs and their linear combinations?

evidence.quote: To reveal this mechanism in full is a standing problem; the impact of topology (in Γ) on arithmetic (in φ(Γ)) will make possible the study of d ≳ 5, so far costly.
What is the group-theoretic and topological mechanism of vanishing for Nambu micro-graphs and their linear combinations ?
